method.scope: Structural relationship of CFA-01 to every registered peer and the Architecture Steward.
method.nonGoal: This dataset does not rank agents, assess their quality, or assign architectural authority.

dimensions.semanticProximity: How directly the peer shares semantic subject matter with World/Ontology/Context.
dimensions.mutualNeed: How strongly each side depends on the other to perform its enduring responsibility.
dimensions.boundaryCoupling: How much ambiguity or contract surface exists at the ownership boundary.
dimensions.worldGraphCoupling: How directly the peer consumes, produces, or transforms World/graph meaning.
dimensions.contextInteractionCoupling: How directly the peer consumes or shapes bounded context.
dimensions.handoffCoupling: Expected frequency of substantive evidence/contract handoffs.
dimensions.externalRealityCoupling: How strongly the peer mediates external-world reality.

scoring.note: Distance is a structural coupling heuristic from CFA-01's perspective. It is not an importance, quality, maturity, or performance score.

method.epistemicStatus: DERIVED from inspected repository foundations; scores are CFA-01 working judgments and should be revisited as peer identities mature.
method.uncertaintyRule: Where a peer lacks a ratified identity or durable state, the relationship is scored from its current bootstrap contract and explicitly marked provisional.

self.name: CFA-01 World / Ontology / Context
self.centralQuestion: What is semantically present in the user's world, how is it related, and how can a bounded purpose-specific slice become Context without becoming a second source of truth?

relationshipClasses.META_STEWARD: Parent/meta-layer that maps and reconciles my semantic work into repository-wide architecture.
relationshipClasses.SEMANTIC_BRIDGE: Peer that translates or preserves meaning across semantic planes directly adjacent to World/Context.
relationshipClasses.CANONICAL_DATA_PARTNER: Peer that keeps durable identity, lineage, persistence and data continuity around my semantic objects.
relationshipClasses.GOVERNANCE_GUARDIAN: Peer that constrains what may be done with World meaning without owning what the meaning is.
relationshipClasses.EXECUTION_CONSUMER: Peer that turns World/Context into durable work and returns outcomes/evidence back toward World.
relationshipClasses.REALIZATION_BRIDGE: Peer that connects canonical semantic capability/world objects to external providers and realizations.
relationshipClasses.ASSEMBLY_COMPOSER: Peer that assembles replaceable pieces which consume World semantics but does not define those semantics.
relationshipClasses.EXPERIENCE_PROJECTION: Peer that turns World meaning into human-facing spaces, surfaces and interaction.
relationshipClasses.CHANGE_CUSTODIAN: Peer that preserves semantic/data/identity continuity when the architecture or product evolves.
relationshipClasses.RUNTIME_SUBSTRATE: Peer providing generic runtime guarantees underneath semantic systems rather than defining their meaning.

distanceBands.name: INNER_RING
distanceBands.meaning: Direct semantic dependency or frequent bidirectional boundary traffic.

distanceBands.name: NEAR_RING
distanceBands.meaning: Strong recurring dependency, usually through a stable seam or lifecycle.

distanceBands.name: MIDDLE_RING
distanceBands.meaning: Important integration partner, but primarily through another responsibility.

distanceBands.name: OUTER_RING
distanceBands.meaning: Important enabling substrate or occasional boundary interaction.

distanceBands.name: REMOTE_RING
distanceBands.meaning: Weak direct coupling; interaction is primarily mediated by other CFAs.

operationalInterpretations.needFromPeer: What CFA-01 needs from this peer as an operating dependency.
operationalInterpretations.needFromMe: What this peer is likely to need from CFA-01 to maintain its own boundary.
operationalInterpretations.evidenceMaturity: 0-5 estimate of how much durable foundation is currently visible in the inspected repository corpus; not a quality ranking.

relationships.name: Architecture Steward
relationships.myRelationship: Parent/meta-steward: it owns repository-wide architectural memory, the documentation model, graph machinery, reconciliation and coordination; I supply semantic World/Context meaning into that system.
needFromPeer: Current responsibility and dependency graph views.
Cross-CFA ownership reconciliation when a semantic seam crosses multiple areas.
Lineage and status discipline for promoting my findings into repository architecture.
Protection against my local model accidentally becoming a second ontology or graph.
needFromMe: Explicit World/Context semantic claims with evidence and epistemic status.
Typed semantic relationships and ownership seams suitable for graph projection.
Early warning when a concept is drifting across CFA boundaries.
Research findings that distinguish canonical meaning from historical/derived implementation.
openQuestions: Exactly how much semantic detail should the Architecture Graph carry before it becomes a second ontology.
What graph projections should consume runtime World semantics once the product graph exists.

relationships.name: Data Steward
relationships.myRelationship: Closest durable data-plane neighbor. I define what a World object/relationship means; Data Steward protects the continuity of that meaning across records, revisions, transformations, persistence and export/restore.
needFromPeer: Clear distinction between semantic identity and record/revision/event identity.
Durable persistence and reconstruction contracts for World objects and relationships.
Lineage-preserving transformations across import, normalization, projection and write-back.
Freshness/revision bases so Context does not silently consume stale canonical state.
needFromMe: Stable semantic definitions for object kinds, relationships, Space and Context references.
Correspondence rules explaining when two source records represent the same World thing.
Semantic lifecycle distinctions that storage must preserve without inventing them.
Clarification of which fields are meaning versus transport/storage metadata.
openQuestions: Exact ownership of semantic identity versus durable record identity.
Minimum continuity payload for Context and graph projections.
Where semantic reconciliation ends and persistence reconciliation begins.

relationships.name: Semantic Continuity Steward
relationships.myRelationship: My strongest semantic peer. It carries meaning from self-knowledge through grounding, command interpretation, canonical Intent/Plan, execution meaning, evidence and representation; I provide the World concepts and relationships onto which those semantic transformations ground.
needFromPeer: A stable understanding of how semantic addresses/phrases map onto World objects and Context.
Cross-plane terminology and CANON discipline so the same World concept is not renamed at each stage.
Grounding/Intent contracts that make clear where World meaning ends and interpretation begins.
Feedback on which World distinctions are actually necessary for deterministic command continuity.
needFromMe: Canonical World nouns, object identities, relation meanings and addressable semantics.
Context semantics that can be referenced by grounding rather than reproduced as prompt prose.
Explicit distinction between World truth, interpretation, representation and authority.
Semantic evolution signals when a World concept changes meaning.
openQuestions: Exact boundary between World address resolution and command interpretation.
How Context candidates become grounded Intent inputs without creating a second ontology.
Shared identity model across World → Intent → Work → Evidence.

relationships.name: Authority / Governance
relationships.myRelationship: Guardian at the meaning-to-permission boundary. I describe what the user/world contains and what relationships are asserted; Authority determines whether an actor may cause a consequential effect involving those things.
needFromPeer: Authority constraints that can be represented as inputs to Context without becoming semantic facts.
Clear scope/principal/delegation semantics so World queries do not accidentally imply permission.
Live authority re-resolution rules for consequential actions.
A clean distinction between world facts and authorization decisions.
needFromMe: Stable identities for the subjects/targets to which authority applies.
Semantic effect descriptions and object relationships needed to understand scope.
Context semantics that identify relevant objects without granting authority.
Warnings when a representation or graph projection is being mistaken for permission.
openQuestions: Principal identity ownership between CFA-02 and CFA-04.
How much risk meaning belongs to Authority versus Capability.
How authority constraints should appear inside candidate Context while remaining non-authoritative.

relationships.name: Agency / Work / Execution
relationships.myRelationship: Downstream execution peer: it turns Intent/Context into durable Work and outcomes; I provide the semantic World substrate needed to know what the work concerns and how resulting changes become World state.
needFromPeer: A durable distinction between Work itself and the World objects Work acts upon.
Outcome/effect records that can be projected back into World meaning without conflating them with execution history.
Work lifecycle and recovery information relevant to current Context.
Evidence linkage from Work outcomes back to changed World objects.
needFromMe: Addressable World targets and relationship semantics.
Context semantics that identify the relevant current state for a Work item.
World-side interpretation of produced artifacts and changed relationships.
Semantic definitions for what counts as a meaningful world update.
openQuestions: When an Outcome becomes a canonical World event/object.
How current Work participates in Context without Context becoming Work state.
Where Work-owned execution events stop and World-owned semantic events begin.

relationships.name: Capability / Provider / Realization
relationships.myRelationship: Bridge between canonical semantic needs and external reality. Provider/Account/Session/Realization are not World semantics, but their observations and effects become important World evidence and relationships.
needFromPeer: Reliable distinctions between provider, account, session, resource and realization.
External observation records that identify what was actually seen or changed.
Realization identity/version information for interpreting provenance and freshness.
Provider knowledge that helps explain whether a World projection reflects current external reality.
needFromMe: Semantic object types and world references that external observations are about.
Source-identity correspondence rules connecting provider identities to canonical World identities.
Context requirements describing which external facts are relevant to a task.
Clear boundary between external observation and canonical World assertion.
openQuestions: How provider observations should enter the World without becoming automatic canonical truth.
Exact boundary between Provider Knowledge and World knowledge.
How external drift is surfaced as a World contradiction or freshness state.

relationships.name: Composition / Plugin / Forge
relationships.myRelationship: Assembly peer. It composes replaceable plugins and capabilities that consume or affect World semantics; it should not become the owner of those semantics.
needFromPeer: A way to declare which World/Context contracts a plugin consumes or contributes.
Composition identity/versioning that can be related to the semantic model it realizes.
Forge/proposal metadata for changes that may alter World-facing behavior.
Symmetry between first-party and third-party pieces so World contracts are not secretly privileged.
needFromMe: Stable semantic contracts that plugins can consume without importing a hidden ontology implementation.
World capability/reference semantics for contributed views or transformations.
Clear distinction between composition metadata and World meaning.
Semantic impact descriptions when a plugin proposes a new object/relationship.
openQuestions: What minimum semantic contract a plugin must declare to participate in World projections.
Where plugin-provided ontology extensions stop and canonical World vocabulary begins.
How composition replacement affects World identity continuity.

relationships.name: Experience / Interaction / Surfaces
relationships.myRelationship: Immediate projection neighbor. It turns World meaning into Spaces, Surfaces, Canvas, focus and interaction; I provide the semantic objects and relationships that those surfaces represent.
needFromPeer: Real interaction requirements that expose which World concepts must be addressable.
Evidence from surface experiments about where users need Space, focus, selection and Context distinctions.
Clear boundary between durable Space semantics and transient Workspace/layout state.
Feedback on whether visual manipulation exposes missing World primitives.
needFromMe: Stable World objects, relationships, Space meaning and addressability.
Projection rules that distinguish canonical state from surface-local layout.
Context semantics that can be seeded from focus/selection without becoming UI truth.
Semantic continuity for direct manipulation and visual intent.
openQuestions: Exact Space versus Workspace boundary.
How surface-generated changes become canonical Intent without bypassing World semantics.
How much Attention belongs to World versus Experience.

relationships.name: Evolution / Compatibility / Self-Maintenance
relationships.myRelationship: Temporal caretaker. I define the semantic identity/relationship continuity that must survive change; Evolution manages the broader change, migration, rollback, quarantine and self-maintenance lifecycle.
needFromPeer: Impact/migration mechanisms that preserve World identity and relationship meaning.
Compatibility analysis for World/Context contract changes.
Detection of stale projections after semantic evolution.
Rollback/recovery paths that do not silently rewrite World history.
needFromMe: Explicit semantic change definitions: shape versus meaning versus identity versus relationship versus projection.
Canonical World/Context contracts that can be versioned and migrated.
Rules identifying which relationships must survive or be reinterpreted.
Semantic falsifiers for proposed self-maintenance changes.
openQuestions: When a changed World concept is migration versus replacement.
How semantic versioning should interact with Data revisions.
How Provider healing/Forge promotion intersects with World semantic evolution.

relationships.name: Runtime Constitution / Core Substrate
relationships.myRelationship: Deep substrate, low semantic proximity. Runtime guarantees admission, isolation, transport, egress, fencing, lifecycle and recovery; I depend on those guarantees but must never let runtime mechanisms define World meaning.
needFromPeer: Stable K0/K1 seams for referring to semantic objects without pulling ontology into K0.
Integrity and isolation guarantees for Lens/context reads.
Recovery/atomicity semantics needed to know when a derived World projection is incomplete.
Clear boundaries so graph/query capabilities remain above substrate guarantees.
needFromMe: Requirements expressed as semantic rather than product-specific runtime needs.
Explicit distinctions between canonical World state and derived/runtime state.
Semantic impact when a substrate guarantee changes observable World continuity.
Falsifiers showing when a runtime mechanism accidentally assumes domain meaning.
openQuestions: Which graph/query operations belong in generic K1 contracts versus plugins.
What runtime guarantees are actually necessary for deterministic Context assembly.
How recovery status should be exposed without becoming World semantics.

ringInterpretation.interpretation: The rings describe semantic/operational coupling to CFA-01, not importance or maturity. A distant peer can still be a hard dependency for particular operations.

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-durable-data seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: semantic identity, relationships, lifecycle meaning and projections must survive persistence and evolution
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: stable semantic contracts and explicit distinction from storage/runtime state

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-intent continuity seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: grounding, intent, authority and work must consume World meaning without redefining it
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: addressable World objects, Context semantics and canonical relationship meaning

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-human surface seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: surface experiments expose missing semantic primitives and Context requirements
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: stable canonical meaning and projection boundaries

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-external-reality seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: observations/effects from external systems become attributable World evidence
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: canonical targets, source correspondence, Context requirements and world-side meaning

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-evolution seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: semantic changes must be classified before migration/replacement
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: stable concepts, identity rules and semantic impact descriptions

majorCrossPeerPatterns.name: World-to-architecture-memory seam
majorCrossPeerPatterns.cfa01Need: repository graph and documentation must preserve the evolving semantic map
majorCrossPeerPatterns.peerNeed: explicit, evidence-backed World/Context concepts and boundaries

immediateOperationalImplications: Treat Data Steward and Semantic Continuity as the two highest-frequency semantic exchange partners.
Treat Experience as a discovery partner: surface behavior can reveal missing World primitives even though Experience does not own them.
Treat Evolution as a standing downstream consumer of World semantic identity and relationship change.
Use Authority, Agency and Capability as distinct boundary consumers rather than collapsing them into World semantics.
Use the Architecture Steward as the repository-level reconciliation layer, never as a semantic substitute.
Use Runtime primarily as a substrate contract; do not ask it to resolve World meaning.
nextRevisionTriggers: A peer receives a ratified Core Agent identity.
A peer publishes a durable core tool/contract.
A cross-CFA boundary is changed by an explicit decision.
The Semantic Lens proof exposes a different coupling pattern.
The product World graph introduces live runtime semantics not represented by the current destination documentation.
